title: Browser DnD game with AI DM
author: CallFromMargin
selftext:
Titles says it all... I made a DnD game with AI DM with VTT-like feel. All the skills, abilities, etc., are coded as a game engine would be, the AI has ability to either use your skills for you (so you can say something like "I throw a fireball without caring about my companions!" or you can just throw a fireball) but it also has ability to roll dice for the enemies, so you can intimidate the enemies, talk with them, scare them, take them prisoners, etc. Absolute majority of game logic is hard coded like rules of any game would be, the AI simply can use game mechanics.

You can try it out of [https://FableFiesta.com](https://fablefiesta.com/)

A bit of specs that might be interesting to y'all. The maps (battlemaps) are created procedurally, each battlemap type has a JSON description HOWEVER I have used bots (mostly GLM) to do extensive research of medieval towns, cities, forts, etc., scrape city atlases from 1500's, ancient Nauraki (really cool bronze age castles), roman fort drawings, etc., and use that as the basis. I have about 5GB of of ancient city drawings on my PC right now, most from 1500 to 1700's. 

I've also used AI to create most of the visual effects for spells, all in all about 700+ effects.

The game rules are hard coded, as would be any game rules, the AI DM can only pick and chose from those rules, yet I very quickly learned that I need to expand the possible number of actions/rules, as the AI often tries to grapple my companions, and then negotiate, or if I let the enemy leave, the AI is scheduling an ambush behind my back, like a true scheming dungeon master... Anyway, still learning from this :) Hope y'all like it.
